rationale: Require available capacity >= demand + reserve (260 + 40 = 300 MW) and N-1 security: after losing the largest committed unit the remainder must still cover demand (>= 260 MW). Combining g1, g2 and g3 gives 120+160+180 = 460 MW; losing the largest unit g3 (180 MW) leaves 280 MW >= 260 MW, so N-1 is satisfied. Cost = (400+80)+(550+100)+(700+120) = 1950 USD. This is the minimum-cost feasible set: any cheaper subset (e.g. g1+g2+g4 = 370 MW leaves only 210 MW after loss; g2+g3+g4 = 430 MW leaves 250 MW) fails N-1, and g1+g3 = 300 MW fails after losing g3.
